Definition: from G5263; an exhibit for imitation or warning (figuratively, specimen, adumbration):--en-(ex-)ample, pattern.
BiblicalUsage: hypódeigma is a plain word for an example, a pattern. In John 13:15, the text says "For I have given you an example." In Hebrews 4:11, the text says "lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief."
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple: hypódeigma tells me that faithfulness is staying when staying is costly — the way God stays with us. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Last Supper; Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
